q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

items.p: The new bridge over the river was designed to be ______: engineers expect it to withstand strong earthquakes and heavy traffic for more than a century without major repairs.
w: Lasting a century contradicts "temporary."
Withstanding earthquakes contradicts "fragile."
The text is about strength, not appearance.
items.e: Withstanding earthquakes and lasting a century describe something durable.

items.p: Because the assembly instructions were so ______, every team in the workshop put the shelves together correctly on the first try, and no one needed to ask the instructor for help.
w: Vague instructions would cause mistakes.
Outdated instructions wouldn't explain the success.
Color doesn't explain why everyone succeeded.
items.e: Everyone succeeding without help shows the instructions were clear.

items.q: As used in the text, what does the word "modest" most nearly mean?
items.p: The music festival drew a modest crowd in its first year, but word spread quickly. By its third year, organizers had to rent a field twice as large to hold everyone who came.
w: "Humble" describes people's attitudes, not crowd size.
"Shy" describes a person's manner.
The text is about size, not cost.
items.e: The contrast with later crowds that needed a larger field shows that "modest" means fairly small.

items.p: Scientists were ______ to find frogs living deep inside the cave, since they had assumed that the cave's air and water were far too cold for any amphibians to survive there.
w: Nothing suggests they had hoped to find frogs.
"Reluctant" means unwilling, which doesn't fit.
They did find the frogs.
items.e: Finding frogs where they assumed none could live would surprise them.

items.p: Although the two paintings look ______ at first glance, close inspection reveals dozens of small differences in color, brushwork, and the placement of figures in the background.
w: "Although" sets up a contrast with the differences, so they must look alike at first.
Damage has nothing to do with the contrast.
Color doesn't set up the contrast with differences.
items.e: "Although" contrasts a first impression with hidden differences, so the paintings look identical at first.

items.p: The committee's decision was ______: it announced that it would not reconsider the proposal, no matter how many letters or petitions residents sent in the coming months.
w: Refusing to reconsider is the opposite of tentative.
Nothing indicates public approval; residents seem to object.
The decision is stated plainly.
items.e: A decision that won't be reconsidered is final.

items.q: As used in the text, what does the word "concrete" most nearly mean?
items.p: The senator's speech was full of sweeping promises, but reporters noted that it offered few concrete plans explaining how any of those promises would actually be kept.
w: That is the literal meaning, not the one used here.
Plans can't be physically heavy.
The contrast is with vagueness, not with change.
items.e: Contrasted with "sweeping promises," concrete plans are specific ones.

items.p: Rather than ______ the author's claims, the reviewer tested each one, checking the cited sources and repeating the key calculations herself before writing a word of her review.
w: Testing the claims is verifying them, so "rather than verifying" contradicts the text.
Publishing doesn't contrast with testing.
The claims were the author's, not the reviewer's.
items.e: "Rather than" contrasts testing the claims with simply accepting them.

items.p: Early critics found the composer's music ______, complaining that its harsh, clashing chords were unpleasant to hear; today, those same chords are admired as bold and inventive.
w: Harsh chords are the opposite of soothing.
The complaint is about harshness, not familiarity.
Length is never discussed.
items.e: "Grating" means irritating to hear, which matches the complaint about harsh, clashing chords.

items.q: As used in the text, what does the phrase "take hold" most nearly mean?
items.p: Researchers hoped the new drought-resistant wheat would thrive in dry regions, but in early field trials it failed to take hold, producing only weak, scattered plants.
w: That is the literal meaning, not the one used for plants.
Crops don't take control.
Harvest comes later; the plants never got established.
items.e: The weak, scattered plants show the wheat failed to become established.

items.p: The documentary takes a ______ approach to its controversial subject, presenting the strongest evidence on each side of the debate without telling viewers which side to believe.
w: Presenting both sides fairly is the opposite of biased.
Tone isn't the point here.
Presenting the strongest evidence is careful, not careless.
items.e: Presenting both sides without taking a position is a balanced approach.

items.p: Though the startup's founders were confident in their product, investors remained ______, waiting to see a full year of sales figures before committing any money to the company.
w: Eager investors wouldn't wait a year.
Waiting before committing doesn't show enthusiasm.
Waiting for sales figures shows interest, so they weren't indifferent.
items.e: Waiting for evidence before investing describes caution.

items.p: Historian Amara Diallo's account of the 1912 textile strike is notably ______: she draws on letters from workers, factory owners, and city officials alike, giving careful attention to each group's perspective.
w: Partisan means favoring one side.
Cursory means hasty, but her attention is careful.
Her account rests on letters, not speculation.
items.e: Giving each group's view careful attention makes the account evenhanded, meaning fair to all sides.

items.p: The poet's late work is often described as ______; after decades of elaborate imagery, she began writing short, plain lines that avoid ornament of any kind.
w: Lavish describes her earlier elaborate style.
Nothing suggests playfulness.
Plain lines are not hard to understand.
items.e: Short, plain, unornamented lines are austere, meaning stark and simple.

items.p: Some economists argue that the policy's benefits have been ______: the predicted rise in employment did occur, but it was far smaller than the policy's supporters had claimed.
w: Supporters promoted the benefits rather than ignoring them.
The actual benefit was smaller than claimed, not larger.
Employment did rise, so the benefits weren't invented.
items.e: A real but smaller-than-claimed benefit was overstated.

items.q: As used in the text, what does the word "conceded" most nearly mean?
items.p: In her review, the critic conceded that the film's pacing was slow, but she argued that its patient camera work rewarded viewers willing to sit with each scene.
w: She didn't give up her argument; she went on to defend the film.
She acknowledged the point rather than refusing it.
Slow pacing is presented as a weakness she grants.
items.e: She admitted a weakness (slow pacing) before making her main argument.

items.p: The researchers' conclusion about the birds' migration routes was ______, since it rested on observations of only three animals tracked during a single, unusually mild season.
w: So little data can't support a definitive conclusion.
The text says nothing about agreement among researchers.
The weakness is the evidence, not relevance.
items.e: A conclusion based on three animals in one season is tenuous, meaning weakly supported.

items.p: Far from being ______, the novel's ending had been planned from the start: early chapters contain small hints that make the final twist seem inevitable on a second reading.
w: "Far from being predictable" doesn't contrast logically with "planned from the start."
The text says the ending seems inevitable, so "far from being inevitable" contradicts it.
Being planned doesn't contrast with being memorable.
items.e: "Far from" sets up a contrast with "planned from the start," which is the opposite of arbitrary.
